buildings.name: Academy
buildings.magicItems: 3 minor scrolls or wondrous items, 2 medium scrolls or wondrous items
buildings.description: An institution of higher learning.

buildings.name: Aerie
buildings.special: +2 bonus to Stability checks against Monster Attacks involving flying monsters.

buildings.name: Alchemist
buildings.special: Base Value +1,000 gp
buildings.description: The laboratory and home of a crafter of poisons, potions, or alchemical items.

buildings.name: Animated Automation
buildings.special: Must be attached to a building which provides a bonus to Productivity

buildings.name: Arena
buildings.description: A large public structure for competitions and team sports.

buildings.name: Assembly
buildings.special: When you issue an improvement edict, you can build one additional building in the settlement containing this building, or one additional terrain improvement in this settlement's hex or the hexes adjacent to it.

buildings.name: Bank
buildings.special: Base value +2,000 gp
buildings.description: A secure building for storing valuables and granting loans.

buildings.name: Bardic College
buildings.description: A center for artistic learning. Education in a Bardic College also includes research into a wide-range of historical topics.

buildings.name: Barracks
buildings.special: Defense +2
buildings.description: A building to house conscripts, guards, militia, soldiers, or similar military forces.

buildings.name: Baths
buildings.limit: Adjacent to Waterway or water border. This limit may be ignored by doubling the cost of the Baths.

buildings.name: Black Market
buildings.special: Base value +2,000 gp
buildings.magicItems: 2 minor items, 1 medium item, 1 major item
buildings.description: A number of shops with secret and usually illegal wares.

buildings.name: Bordello
buildings.special: Each Bordello causes a -1 penalty to Stability checks to resist Drug Den or Plague events.

buildings.name: Brewery
buildings.description: A building for beer brewing, winemaking, or some similar use.

buildings.name: Brickyard
buildings.special: Quarries in the this settlement's hex or adjacent hexes is reduced to 6 BP. Also, quarries in those hexes generate 1 additional BP per 2 quarries. A quarry may only benefit from one Brickyard at a time.

buildings.name: Bridge
buildings.special: Shares the space with a river or Waterway lot
buildings.description: Allows travel across a river or Waterway, easing transportation

buildings.name: Bureau
buildings.description: A large warren of offices for clerks and record-keepers working for a guild or government.

buildings.name: Caster's Tower
buildings.description: The home and laboratory for a spellcaster

buildings.name: Castle
buildings.special: Defense +8
buildings.description: The home of the settlement’s leader or the heart of its defenses

buildings.name: Cathedral
buildings.special: Halves Consumption increase for Promotion edicts
buildings.magicItems: 3 minor potions or wondrous items,2 medium potions or wondrous items
buildings.description: The focal point of the settlement’s spiritual leadership

buildings.name: Cistern
buildings.limit: NOT adjacent to a Dump, Graveyard, Stable, Stockyard or Tannery
buildings.special: Can share lot with another building
buildings.description: Contains a safe supply of fresh water for the settlement

buildings.name: City Wall
buildings.special: Defense +1
buildings.description: A fortification of one side of a district with a sturdy wall. The GM may allow for cliffs and other natural features to function as a City Wall for one or more sides of a district. You may construct gates through your own city wall at no cost.

buildings.name: Colossus
buildings.special: Your Armies in the same hex as the Colossus gain a +1 bonus to Morale. If they are in the settlement, this bonus increases to +2. The Colossus can share the same space as either a Lighthouse or an Observatory

buildings.name: Crematorium
buildings.special: +2 bonus on Stability checks against Plague events or Monster Attacks involving undead.

buildings.name: Dance Hall
buildings.description: An establishment for dancing, drinking, carousing, and holding celebrations

buildings.name: Deathless Laborers
buildings.special: Must be attached to a building which provides a bonus to Productivity

buildings.name: Dump
buildings.limit: Cannot be adjacent to House, Mansion, or Noble Villa
buildings.description: A centralized place to dispose of refuse

buildings.name: Everflowing Spring
buildings.limit: Settlement must have a building that can create medium magic items
buildings.special: Can share lot with Castle, Cathedral, Market, Monument, Park, or Town Hall
buildings.description: A fountain built around several decanters of endless water that provides an inexhaustible supply of fresh water

buildings.name: Exotic Artisan
buildings.magicItems: 1 minor ring, wand, or wondrous item
buildings.description: The shop and home of a jeweler, tinker, glassblower, or the like

buildings.name: Forbiddance
buildings.special: Prerequisite: Cathedral. Unrest increases by 1d4.

buildings.name: Foreign Quarter
buildings.special: Increase the value of trade routes (see Trade Edicts on page 232) by 5% (maximum 100%)
buildings.description: An area with many foreigners, as well as shops and services catering to them

buildings.name: Foundry
buildings.special: Increase the Economy and BP earned per turn by 1 for 1 Mine connected to this settlement by a river or Road
buildings.description: Processes ore and refines it into finished metal

buildings.name: Gambling Den
buildings.special: Each Gambling Den causes a -1 penalty to Stability checks to resist Drug Den events.
buildings.magicItems: 1 Magic item (roll d%: 1-80, minor item; 81-98, medium item; 99-100, major item)
buildings.description: An illicit place for games of skill and chance, wagering all manner of stakes.

buildings.name: Garrison
buildings.description: A large building to house armies, train guards, and recruit militia

buildings.name: Granary
buildings.special: If Farms reduce Consumption below 0, store up to 5 BP of excess prod. for use later when Consumption exceeds the Treasury
buildings.description: A place to store grain and food.

buildings.name: Graveyard
buildings.description: A plot of land to honor and bury the dead

buildings.name: Guildhall
buildings.special: Base value +1,000 gp
buildings.description: The headquarters for a guild or similar organization

buildings.name: Hallow/Unhallow
buildings.special: Prerequisite: Cathedral, Sacred Grove, or Temple

buildings.name: Hanging Gardens
buildings.special: Reduces consumption in the city by 1.

buildings.name: Herbalist
buildings.description: The workshop and home of a gardener, healer, or poisoner

buildings.name: Hospital
buildings.special: Increase Stability by 2 during plague events
buildings.description: A building devoted to healing the sick

buildings.name: House
buildings.special: The first House you build during the Improvement phase does not count against the total number of buildings you can build during the phase
buildings.description: A number of mid-sized houses for citizens

buildings.name: Inn
buildings.special: Base value +500 gp
buildings.description: A place for visitors to rest

buildings.name: Jail
buildings.description: A fortified structure for confining criminals or dangerous monsters

buildings.name: Library
buildings.description: A large building containing an archive of books

buildings.name: Lighthouse
buildings.limit: 1 per settlement, must be on a water border at the edge of a district grid
buildings.special: The cost to create Fisheries in hexes adjacent to the settlement is reduced to 3 BP. Trade routes from settlements with lighthouse count water hexes as one-quarter (rather than one-half) when calculating the Trade Route Length.

buildings.name: Lumberyard
buildings.limit: The cost to construct Sawmills in the settlement hex and hexes adjacent is reduced to 2 BP. Also, Sawmills in those hexes generate 1 additional BP per 2 Sawmills. A Sawmill may only benefit from one Lumberyard.

buildings.name: Luxury Store
buildings.special: Base value +2,000 gp
buildings.magicItems: 2 minor rings, wands, or wondrous items
buildings.description: A shop that specializes in expensive comforts for the wealthy

buildings.name: Magic Shop
buildings.special: Base value +2,000 gp
buildings.magicItems: 4 minor wondrous items, 2 medium wondrous items, 1 major wondrous item
buildings.description: A shop that specializes in magic items and spells

buildings.name: Magical Academy
buildings.magicItems: 3 minor potions, scrolls, or wondrous items;1 medium potion, scroll, or wondrous item
buildings.description: An institution for training students in spellcasting, magic item crafting, and various arcane arts

buildings.name: Magical Alarms
buildings.special: Prerequisite: Caster's Tower

buildings.name: Magical Streetlamps
buildings.limit: Settlement must have a Cathedral,Magic Shop, Magical Academy or Temple
buildings.special: Can share a lot with any building or improvement
buildings.description: Continual flame lamps that illuminate the lot

buildings.name: Mansion
buildings.description: A single huge manor housing a rich family and its servants

buildings.name: Market
buildings.special: Base value +2,000 gp
buildings.description: An open area for traveling merchants and bargain hunters

buildings.name: Menagerie
buildings.special: Increase Loyalty by 1/4 the CR of the highest-CR creature in the Menagerie
buildings.description: A large park stocked with exotic creatures for public viewing

buildings.name: Military Academy
buildings.special: Armies and commanders recruited at the settlement gain one bonus tactic
buildings.magicItems: 1 minor armor, shield, or weapon; 1 medium armor, shield, or weapon
buildings.description: An institution dedicated to the study of war and the training of elite soldiers and officers

buildings.name: Mill
buildings.special: With GM approval, you can construct a windmill at the same cost without the water district border requirement
buildings.description: A building used to cut lumber or grind grain

buildings.name: Mint
buildings.description: A secure building where the kingdom’s coinage is minted and standard weights and measures are kept

buildings.name: Moat
buildings.special: Defense +1; cannot be damaged by siege engines
buildings.description: A fortification of one side of a district with an open or water-filled ditch, often backed by a low dike or embankment. The GM may allow a river or similar natural feature to function as a moat for one or more sides of a district

buildings.name: Monastery
buildings.description: A cloister for meditation, study, and the pursuit of various other scholarly paths

buildings.name: Monument
buildings.description: A local memorial such as a bell tower, a statue of a settlement founder, a large tomb, or a public display of art

buildings.name: Museum
buildings.description: A place to display art and artifacts both modern and historical. The GM may allow the kingdom leaders to display a valuable item (such as a magic item or bejeweled statue) in the museum, increasing Fame during this display by 1 for every 10,000 gp of the item’s price (maximum +5 Fame), and by an additional 1 if the item is significant to the kingdom’s history

buildings.name: Noble Villa
buildings.description: A sprawling manor with luxurious grounds that houses a noble’s family and staff

buildings.name: Observatory
buildings.description: A dome or tower with optical devices for viewing the heavens

buildings.name: Orphanage
buildings.description: A place for housing and taking care of large numbers of orphans

buildings.name: Palace
buildings.special: Base value +1,000 gp; you may make two special edicts per turn (see page 229), but take a –2 penalty on kingdom checks associated with each special edict
buildings.description: A grand edifice and walled grounds demonstrating one’s wealth, power, and authority to the world

buildings.name: Park
buildings.description: A plot of land set aside for its serene beauty

buildings.name: Paved Streets
buildings.description: Brick or stone pavement that speeds transportation

buildings.name: Permanent Teleportation Circle
buildings.special: Prerequisite: Caster's Tower, Magic Shop, and Magical Academy

buildings.name: Pier
buildings.special: Base value +1,000 gp
buildings.description: Warehouses and workshops for docking ships and handling cargo and passengers

buildings.name: Private Sanctum
buildings.special: Increase the DC of Espionage Edicts against your kingdom by +2 per block. Prerequisites: Caster's Tower and Magical Academy

buildings.name: Sacred Grove
buildings.limit: Adjacent to Park or a city district border with no City Wall or Moat
buildings.special: +2 bonus to Stability checks against Crop Failure events or Monster Attacks involving animals, plants or fey. +1 bonus to Stability checks to resist Plague events

buildings.name: Sewer System
buildings.description: An underground sanitation system that keeps the settlement clean, though it may become home to criminals and monsters

buildings.name: Shop
buildings.special: Base value +500 gp
buildings.description: A general store

buildings.name: Shrine
buildings.magicItems: 1 minor potion, scroll, or wondrous item
buildings.description: A shrine, idol, sacred grove, or similar holy site designed for worship by pious individuals

buildings.name: Smithy
buildings.description: The workshop of an armorsmith, blacksmith, weaponsmith, or other craftsman who works with metal

buildings.name: Stable
buildings.limit: Adjacent to 1 House, Mansion, or Noble Villa
buildings.special: Base value +500 gp
buildings.description: A structure for housing or selling horses and other mounts

buildings.name: Stockyard
buildings.special: Farms in this hex or adjacent hexes reduce Consumption by 3 instead of 2
buildings.description: Barns and pens that store herd animals and prepare them for nearby slaughterhouses

buildings.name: Tannery
buildings.limit: Cannot be adjacent to House,Mansion, Noble Villa, or TenementCannot be adjacent to House,Mansion, Noble Villa, or Tenement
buildings.description: A structure that prepares hides and leather

buildings.name: Tavern
buildings.special: Base value +500 gp
buildings.description: An eating or drinking establishment

buildings.name: Temple
buildings.description: A large place of worship dedicated to a deity

buildings.name: Tenement
buildings.special: Counts as House for buildings that must be adjacent to a House
buildings.description: A staggering number of low-rent housing units

buildings.name: Theater
buildings.discount: Brothel, Exotic Artisan, Inn, Park, Tavern
buildings.description: A venue for entertainments such as plays, operas, and concerts

buildings.name: Town Hall
buildings.description: A public venue for town meetings, repository for town records, and offices for minor bureaucrats

buildings.name: Trade Shop
buildings.special: Base value +500 gp
buildings.description: A shop front for a tradesperson, such as a baker, butcher, candle maker, cobbler, rope maker, or wainwright

buildings.name: Tunnels
buildings.special: Tunnels are underground and do not occupy a lot on the surface, but each runs underneath one city square of 4 lots. You can pass through the square of an impassable building by moving through the Tunnels underneath it.

buildings.name: University
buildings.discount: Academy, Bardic College, Library, Magical Academy, Military Academy, Museum
buildings.magicItems: 4 minor scrolls or wondrous items,2 medium scrolls or wondrous items
buildings.description: An institution of higher learning, focusing mainly on mundane subjects but dabbling in magical theory

buildings.name: Warehouse
buildings.limit: Adjacent to water border or Guildhall, Market, Pier, Trade Shop, or Waterfront

buildings.name: Watchtower
buildings.special: Defense +2
buildings.description: A tall structure that serves as a guard post

buildings.name: Waterfront
buildings.discount: Black Market, Guildhall, Market, Pier, Warehouse
buildings.limit: Adjacent to water district border,1 per settlement
buildings.special: Base value +4,000 gp; halves Loyalty penalty for Taxation edicts
buildings.magicItems: 2 minor wondrous items, 1 medium wondrous item, 1 major wondrous item
buildings.description: A port for waterborne arrival and departure, with facilities for shipping and shipbuilding

buildings.name: Watergate
buildings.special: Shares City Wall
buildings.description: A gate in a City Wall that allows water (such as a river, Aqueduct, or Waterway) to enter the settlement. A Watergate has underwater defenses to block unwanted access. If you construct a Watergate when you construct a City Wall, the Watergate does not count toward the limit of the number of buildings you can construct per turn

buildings.name: Waterway
buildings.special: Counts as water district border for adjacent buildings
buildings.description: A river or canal occuping part of the District Grid. At the GM’s option, a natural Waterway may already exist on the grid, requiring no action or BP to build. If you construct a City Wall that touches or crosses the Waterway, you must also build Watergates on the same turn

buildings.name: Windmill
buildings.special: A Windmill adjacent to a Cistern or Granary increases the Stability bonus provided by that building by +1

terrain.name: Aqueduct*
terrain.terrain: One end must be hill or mountain hex; can pass through any type of hex
terrain.effect: Loyalty+1, Stability +1, allows settlement to build water-dependent buildings
terrain.cost: As a Road, except the cost is not doubled for hexes with rivers (See Table 4–6: Terrain Imp. On page 214)
terrain.description: An Aqueduct brings water from alpine lakes and rivers to lowland cities where water is scarce or insufficient for the local populace. A finished series of Aqueduct hexes must connect to a hill or mountain hex (with a river or lake) on one end and a settlement on the other end; otherwise, youdo not gain its benefit.

terrain.name: Bridge*
terrain.cost: When you build a Road in a hex that contains a river, the doubled coast of the Road includes the cost of bridges needed to cross the river. You don’t need to build a Bridge as a separate unit; it’s listed here for reference only
terrain.description: A Bridge allows your Road hexes to cross rivers

terrain.name: Canal*
terrain.effect: Settlements in a hex with a Canal treat the hex as if it had a river
terrain.description: A Canal is an artificial waterway that allows barge traffic to haul heavy commodities

terrain.name: Farm*
terrain.terrain: Desert (requires canal, coastline, or river), hill, or plain
terrain.description: A Farm helps feed your kingdom

terrain.name: Fishery*
terrain.description: A Fishery is like a Farm, except it provides abundant fish rather than planted crops

terrain.name: Fort*
terrain.effect: Stability +2, Defense +4, increase Consumption by 1 BP;Unrest decreases by 1 when completed.If this hex becomes a settlement, this improvement counts as one Barracks and one Stables building
terrain.description: A Fort is a walled encampment for military forces outside a settlement. You can upgrade a Watchtower to a Fort (Unrest decreases when you do so, just as if you had built the Fort from scratch)

terrain.name: Highway*
terrain.effect: Economy +1 for every 4 hexes of Highway, Stability +1 for every 8 hexes of Highway;Improves overland travel speed (Pathfinder RPG Core Rulebook 172
terrain.cost: Twice the cost of a Road (See Table 4–6: Terrain Imp. On page 214)
terrain.description: A highway is a paved and well-maintained version of a Road. You may upgradea Road into a Highway. Kingdom Size must be 26 or greater to build a Highway

terrain.name: Mine
terrain.effect: Economy +1, earn +1 BP per turn when collecting taxes during the Income phase
terrain.description: A Mine extracts metal, coal, salt, or other useful materials from the earth

terrain.name: Quarry
terrain.effect: Stability +1, earn +1 BP per turn when collecting taxes during the Income phase
terrain.description: A Quarry extracts workable stone from the ground

terrain.name: Road*
terrain.effect: Economy +1 for every 4 hexes of Road, Stability +1 for every 8 hexes of Road;improves overland travel speed (Core Rulebook 172)
terrain.cost: See the Road column of Table 4–6: Terrain Imp. On page 214
terrain.description: A Road speeds travel through your kingdom and promotes trade. You can upgrade a Road to a Highway

terrain.name: Sawmill
terrain.effect: Stability +1, earn +1 BP per turn when collecting taxes during the Income phase
terrain.description: A sawmill centralizes the activities of loggers and turns trees into lumber for use in building and crafting

terrain.name: Watchtower*
terrain.effect: Stability +1, Defense +2; Unrest decreases by 1 when completed.If this hex becomes a settlement, this improvement counts as a Watchtower
terrain.description: A Watchtower flies your f lag, is a safe place for your patrols, and establishes your power on the frontier. A Watchtower cannot share a hex with a Fort or another Watchtower
